remediation_v4.defect: validation_v4 FAIL_V4, a REAL security hole: the flight-recorder route group had no authorization at all, and record_native_editor_event trusted caller-supplied actor_id/workspace_id from the JSON body and persisted them into authoritative PostgreSQL/EventLedger/Flight Recorder attribution. An unauthenticated caller could forge actor/workspace-attributed events or read recorder data across workspaces. The declared proof command also ran ZERO tests because it omitted the feature gate, a false green.

security_boundary_implemented.middleware: authorize_flight_recorder_request installed with middleware::from_fn_with_state over the ENTIRE route group before with_state, mirroring the proven api::memory pattern. Authenticates via stage::capture_context (live native-MCP binding token + process-birth identity) -> 401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION. Resolves one capability per route class via capability_registry.profile_can -> 403 HSK-403-FR-CAPABILITY. Emits one redacted capability_action FR event for EVERY allow and deny; audit-write failure fails the request CLOSED with 500. Injects a RecorderAuthority request extension so handlers read identity only from there, never from headers or body.
security_boundary_implemented.capabilities: fr.read (existing) plus new fr.read.global, fr.ingest.runtime_chat, fr.ingest.native_editor. Operator receives the three scoped ones. fr.read.global is deliberately granted to NO profile, so unscoped cross-workspace enumeration is fail-closed. KERNEL_BUILDER verified it is defined but absent from the grant list.
security_boundary_implemented.routes: The unscoped POST /flight_recorder/{native_editor_event,runtime_chat_event} paths are REMOVED. Both are now POST /workspaces/:workspace_id/flight_recorder/... so the path itself is the workspace authority, validated against a real canonical workspace row before any write. An unknown workspace returns the same 403 HSK-403-FR-WORKSPACE as unauthorized, so existence is never disclosed.
security_boundary_implemented.envelope_contract: actor_id / actor_kind / workspace_id are no longer client authority. Optional; if present they must EXACTLY match the authenticated context or the request is rejected before any durable write; if absent the server fills them. Canonicalization overwrites them from context BEFORE validate_document_save_receipt, so a save receipt can only be claimed by the principal that minted it.
security_boundary_implemented.idempotency: workspace_scoped_fr_event_id(workspace_id, client_event_id), a deterministic SHA-256-derived RFC 9562 v8 UUID, is now the durable FR/EventLedger identity; aggregate id and idempotency keys carry the workspace. Cross-workspace event-id pre-emption can no longer create a conflict, be read back, or be reconciled. The ack returns both event_id (client) and fr_event_id (durable).
security_boundary_implemented.reads: GET /flight_recorder and /events require fr.read; omitting or blanking the wsid query additionally requires fr.read.global -> 403 and audited. The authenticated scope is applied LAST and UNCONDITIONALLY after every other filter, so no actor/actor_id/surface/event_type/event_id combination can widen it; a cross-workspace event_id returns 200 with an empty list rather than an error.

fail_report.summary: MT-109 FAIL V4. The memory routes have capability middleware, but the flight-recorder route group does not. GET /flight_recorder, GET /events, POST /flight_recorder/runtime_chat_event, and POST /flight_recorder/native_editor_event are merged directly into api::mod with no global or route-local authorization. record_native_editor_event trusts caller-supplied actor_id and workspace_id from the JSON body and writes them to PostgreSQL/EventLedger and the Flight Recorder. An unauthenticated caller can therefore forge actor/workspace-attributed events or read recorder data. No native-editor authorization negative test exists. The documented/default cargo filter executes zero tests unless an undeclared feature is added, and the correctly featured current-head run did not finish compiling inside the five-minute validation bound.
fail_report.acceptance_impact: AC-109-1 cannot pass because authenticated actor/workspace attribution is part of a trustworthy authority store; strict JSON shape and idempotency do not make unauthenticated writes acceptable. AC-109-4's targeted-test gate is unproved at current HEAD: the ordinary command is a zero-test false green and the real feature-gated suite was not executed. The unauthenticated GET routes also expose cross-workspace recorder data.
failure_evidence: flight_recorder::routes attaches no middleware and directly exposes two GET and two POST routes before with_state(state).
api::mod merges flight_recorder_routes without a global authorization layer.
record_native_editor_event accepts State plus Json only; it has no HeaderMap, authenticated context, request extension, capability check, workspace membership check, or allow/deny audit decision.
The handler merely rejects empty actor_id/workspace_id, then trims and persists those caller-controlled values into the authoritative EventLedger/Flight Recorder attribution.

By contrast, memory::routes applies authorize_memory_request, derives capture_context, checks capability_registry.profile_can, writes a capability decision event, and returns 401/403 on denial. The same security boundary is absent for native ingestion and recorder reads.
The native-editor test inventory has no unauthorized, missing-binding, spoofed-actor, cross-workspace, denied-capability, or authorization-audit test for the HTTP route.
cargo test --lib native_editor completed successfully but ran 0 tests and filtered out 1875 because the route tests are gated by cfg(all(test, feature = 'duckdb-flight-recorder')).
The correctly featured api::flight_recorder::tests::native_editor command exceeded a five-minute compile bound without starting a test; it is NOT_EXECUTED, not a product test failure or pass.

remediation_plan: 1. Define explicit capabilities for recorder read, runtime-chat ingest, and native-editor ingest in the canonical capability registry. Apply fail-closed middleware to the entire flight-recorder route group, reusing the authenticated capture_context/capability-decision pattern already proven in api::memory.

2. Stop trusting body-supplied actor_id. Derive the durable actor identity and actor kind from the authenticated request/session context. Either reject an envelope actor_id that does not exactly match the context or remove it from client authority and overwrite it server-side; document the chosen canonical envelope contract.

3. Bind workspace authority. Prefer a workspace-scoped ingestion route such as /workspaces/:workspace_id/flight_recorder/native_editor_event, or otherwise validate the body workspace_id against an authenticated allowed-workspace claim before any pending receipt or FR write. Reject cross-workspace attempts before durable mutation.

4. Protect GET /flight_recorder and /events with read capability plus workspace/surface filtering. Do not allow an authenticated caller to omit scope and enumerate other workspaces unless an explicit higher capability authorizes global recorder access; audit every allow/deny decision.

5. Partition idempotency/conflict ownership by authenticated workspace/tenant as required by authority. Prove a caller cannot pre-seed another workspace's event_id, convert its retry into a conflict, read its event, or complete/reconcile its pending receipt.

6. Add HTTP-level authorization tests using the real router: missing binding/token -> 401 and zero residue; valid context without capability -> 403 and zero residue; spoofed actor/body workspace -> rejection; cross-workspace replay -> rejection; valid capability -> accepted with server-derived attribution; every decision produces the exact redacted capability audit event.

7. Apply the same tests to runtime_chat_event and both recorder GET aliases so the route group has one coherent boundary. Verify query filters cannot bypass workspace scope and errors do not disclose protected event existence.

8. Make the declared proof command execute nonzero tests by default or explicitly record --features duckdb-flight-recorder in the authoritative proof targets and CI profile. Add a guard that fails if the MT-109 filter matches zero tests; do not accept '0 passed, 0 failed' as green.

9. Rerun the full native-editor ingestion and memory suites against isolated real PostgreSQL with deterministic schema cleanup. Preserve strict payload/kind validation, EventLedger-first reconciliation, idempotency, no read amplification, proposal provenance, review-gated commit, FR-EVT-MEM shapes, and commit-outbox recovery.

10. Run cargo check/test with the required feature profile in the canonical external target, capture nonzero counts and exact source SHA, and return READY_FOR_VALIDATION only after an independent security review confirms no unauthenticated read/write or caller-forged attribution remains.

remediation_steps: 1. Replace FR_CAPABILITY_PROFILE plus existence-only workspace authorization with the canonical authenticated authority context. Carry LocalAccount, acting Principal, immutable session, active AccessSpace, and delegation identity from the verified binding into RecorderAuthority; do not infer a fixed Operator profile from possession of a binding token.

2. Route every recorder workspace decision through the Handshake ResourceBroker (or the current canonical equivalent implementing ResourceGrant semantics). Require the exact read or ingest action capability AND an effective grant for the target workspace/resource. Missing membership, missing grant, wrong Space, revoked grant, stale session, or mismatched delegation must deny before querying or mutating Flight Recorder/EventLedger.

3. Apply resource authorization uniformly to both GET aliases and both workspace-scoped POST routes. GET with wsid must authorize that wsid before state.flight_recorder.list_events. POST must authorize the path workspace before any capability audit, pending EventLedger receipt, reconciliation enqueue, or recorder write that could disclose or mutate protected state.

4. Preserve the existing V4 hardening: strict envelopes, server-derived actor identity, path/body workspace equality, workspace-partitioned event IDs, constant-shape cross-workspace misses, fail-closed audit writes, SurrealDB/EventLedger-first ordering, idempotent retry, and no unscoped global reads for ordinary profiles.

5. Ensure the underlying SurrealDB access used for protected rows executes with authenticated record-user context and SCHEMAFULL table/field PERMISSIONS. Privileged AppState handles may be used for setup/maintenance only and cannot be the ordinary request or isolation-proof path.

6. Add real-router adversarial tests with two accounts, two Principals, two AccessSpaces, and at least two workspaces/resources. Cover: wrong account, wrong Space, project member without ResourceGrant, valid capability without grant, valid grant without capability, revoked/expired grant, stale session after Space switch, forged wsid/path/body, cross-workspace event-id preemption, and unauthorized GET filters. Require constant-shape denial or empty results as specified and zero protected mutation/read leakage.

Add positive least-privilege tests proving a caller with both the exact route capability and target ResourceGrant can ingest/read only that workspace; verify server-derived attribution records account, Principal, session, Space, resource, and delegation identifiers in EventLedger/Flight Recorder without leaking secrets.

8. Add revocation tests that authorize, revoke or reduce the grant/Space while the session exists, and prove subsequent reads/writes are denied within the specified policy window with cached authorization re-evaluated.

9. Retain current MemoryPack/proposal behavior and re-run its side-effect-free read, provenance, review-gated mutation, crash/restart, strict schema, and EventLedger tests so the recorder authorization repair does not regress AC-109-2/3.

independent_findings.summary: All MT-109 protected route families authorize a global capability profile but not the selected workspace resource.
evidence: src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/flight_recorder.rs:350-406 resolves a process binding, checks the fixed Operator profile, and inserts RecorderAuthority without an account, Principal, AccessSpace, ResourceGrant, or resource decision.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/flight_recorder.rs:410-422 defines workspace authorization as existence only; src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/flight_recorder.rs:1329-1360 and 1524-1583 use that missing boundary for writes and reads.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/memory.rs:171-252 resolves the same process binding, checks profile_can(Operator, capability), writes derived actor headers, and never authorizes the path workspace resource.
src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/memory.rs:456-500,698-710,1055-1061 reaches workspace and FEMS state after only workspace existence checks.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/capabilities.rs:217-238 globally grants recorder and memory actions to Operator; the Master Spec explicitly says CapabilityProfile cannot substitute for content visibility or ResourceGrant.
independent_findings.failure_scenario: Any process that holds the live native binding token can substitute the identifier of another existing workspace and read or mutate its recorder and FEMS resources because the selected workspace is never checked against a current grant.

independent_findings.summary: The required identity/session/resource-authorization substrate does not exist, so MT-109 cannot be safely repaired as a local middleware edit.
evidence: A product-wide source scan finds zero ResourceBroker, ResourceGrant, AccessSpace, or LocalAccount type definitions and no corresponding Surreal tables; Principal appears only in an unrelated Atelier-local context.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/stage.rs:132-140 and 449-490 defines CaptureContext only from token, PID, and process-birth identity; it has no persisted account, Principal, selected Space, grant, expiry, revocation epoch, or policy version.

src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/binding.rs:48-89 serializes only endpoint, token, PID, and process-birth identity. It is a local process/UI-steering credential, not a backend-authenticated account session.
src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/mod.rs:312-323 gives Workspace only id, name, and timestamps with no protected-resource owner or grant linkage.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql:63-75 defines workspaces without owner/session/Space/resource metadata; lines 800-829 and 4922-5013 define EventLedger and FEMS tables as PERMISSIONS NONE with no authenticated record-user policy or required authority fields.
No other WP-KERNEL-012 MT contract owns ResourceBroker, ResourceGrant, AccessSpace, LocalAccount, AuthenticatedSession, ProtectedResource, or record-user implementation.
independent_findings.failure_scenario: A coder follows FAIL_V6 literally and creates an MT-109-local grant shim or trusts new client claims. The code compiles and route tests pass, but ordinary storage still runs privileged, other MT-109 routes remain bypassable, revocation cannot work, and the claimed ResourceBroker boundary is only a renamed existence check.

hard_predecessor.reason: MT-109 consumes ProtectedResources but the shared authority substrate required by current Master Spec does not exist. Build and independently prove that substrate before accepting MT-109 route integration.
hard_predecessor.scope_rule: This is cross-cutting product work required by current Master Spec, not an MT-109-local invention. Keep it as a separately reviewable predecessor change/range even if the Operator elects to carry it in the same feature branch. Do not weaken MT-109 or rewrite the spec to avoid it.
minimum_modules: src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/authority.rs (new): one reusable async authentication and authorization middleware/service boundary; no route-local duplicate policy engines.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/stage.rs: stop converting possession of the MCP binding into an Operator identity; resolve an opaque credential to the persisted authenticated session and retain process binding only as an additional channel-binding check.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/mod.rs: typed LocalAccount, Principal, AuthenticatedSession, AccessSpace, ProtectedResource, ResourceGrant, resource action, policy version, revocation epoch, and authorization-decision contracts exposed through the storage boundary.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/resource_authority.rs (new) and src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/mod.rs: canonical persisted authentication/session lookup and ResourceBroker evaluation using current database state, exact resource, exact action, Space filter, capability, expiry, revocation, account status, and delegation constraints.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql and schema.rs: SCHEMAFULL account/principal/session/Space/protected-resource/grant records with UUID-v7 links, token hashes rather than raw secrets, expiry/revocation/policy epochs, workspace ownership/resource linkage, explicit record-user table/field permissions, and migration/bootstrap coverage.
src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/workspaces.rs: create/read workspaces through the ProtectedResource envelope and owner/grant invariants rather than an unowned id/name row.
src/backend/handshake_core/tests/resource_authority_tests.rs (new or canonical existing test target): real embedded SurrealDB record-user and ResourceBroker positive/negative/concurrency proof.
required_behavior: Issue bounded server-side AuthenticatedSessions for persisted LocalAccounts and Principals. The client receives only an opaque credential; account, Principal, Space, roles, grants, delegation, expiry, and policy claims are server-resolved and cannot be supplied or widened by request headers/body/path.

Represent each workspace and its protected children through stable ProtectedResource rows or a canonical registry link. Creation establishes private owner access; membership and capability alone do not grant content visibility.

ResourceBroker evaluates the exact action and resource against a live session, enabled account, selected Space, current ResourceGrant set, MembershipRole where relevant, CapabilityProfile, delegation intersection, expiry, revocation epoch, and policy version. Missing or malformed state denies.

Ordinary protected queries use an authenticated SurrealDB record-user context whose table and sensitive-field PERMISSIONS enforce the same boundary. Privileged storage handles are limited to bootstrap/maintenance and are rejected as ordinary-route or isolation proof.

Background reconciliation uses an explicit least-privilege service Principal and grant. It may repair only already-authorized scoped outbox rows and must not enumerate or mutate all accounts through the ordinary route path.

Security audit events carry account_id, principal_id, session_id, access_space_id, delegation chain, exact resource ref, action, result, and policy version, while denial responses and emitted observability do not disclose protected existence.

Use the shared authority middleware for both Flight Recorder GET aliases, both recorder POST routes, MemoryPack reads, proposal create/list/get/artifact/review/commit, commit-report reads, item counts, and reconciliation entrypoints.

Require both the route action capability and an effective grant for the exact workspace/resource before the first protected read, allow audit, pending receipt, outbox enqueue, EventLedger append, recorder write, proposal mutation, review, or commit.

Never accept workspace/account/Principal/Space/role/grant claims from request fields as authority. Path and body IDs are selectors only; mismatches and foreign-but-existing resources use constant-shape denial or empty results as the route contract specifies.

Scope every Flight Recorder, EventLedger, FEMS pack/proposal/item/report/outbox row to the ProtectedResource envelope and persist full redacted attribution. Resource-specific grant changes and Space switches must affect subsequent reads/writes within the bounded policy window.

Preserve the valid MT-109 behavior already present: closed versioned event vocabulary, deny_unknown_fields, payload bounds, server actor attribution, workspace-partitioned idempotency, EventLedger-first recovery, MemoryPack field parity and side-effect-free reads, provenance-required proposals, review gating, immutable committed memory before approval, deterministic replay, and no PostgreSQL/SQLite path.

Do not change src/frontend/** inside MT-109. Expose the backend session/authority contract for the separately owned native-client pairing; before whole-WP closeout that client must obtain and present the backend-issued opaque session rather than treating the MCP process token as account authority.

adversarial_tests: Real mounted-router matrix with two accounts, two Principals, two AccessSpaces, two workspaces, a same-project private resource, and independent capabilities/grants. Prove capability-without-grant, grant-without-capability, wrong account, wrong Space, member-without-resource-grant, disabled account, expired/revoked session, changed grant, stale Space, and mismatched delegation all deny before protected read/write with zero residue.

Exercise every MT-109 route, not only Flight Recorder: both GET aliases, both ingestion POSTs, MemoryPack, proposal create/list/get/artifact/review/commit, commit report, item count, and background reconciliation.

Authenticate as SurrealDB record users and attempt SELECT, CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, UPSERT/conflict, bulk, outbox, and recovery bypasses on workspaces, kernel_event_ledger, FEMS tables, and recorder projection tables. Run privileged setup separately and prove it is not used for ordinary route execution.

Authorize a request, then revoke/expire/reduce its grant, disable its account, and switch its Space while the session remains live. Prove cached or open contexts cannot continue after the bounded policy window.

Probe foreign IDs through wsid, event_id, actor, actor_id, surface, event_type, proposal_id, commit_id, scope_key, malformed values, blank scope, and concurrent same client event IDs. Require no existence/count/timing/error-shape leakage and isolated idempotency.

Regression-run strict event decoding, all documented native/interop kinds, failure-window reconciliation, MemoryPack shape/no-write-amplification, proposal provenance, review-gated commit, FR-EVT-MEM-001..005, and committed-memory immutability.
validator_proof: At the exact clean remediation commit, validator executes a nonzero focused identity/ResourceBroker/record-user proof first; no MT-109 route suite may count as green while that predecessor is red.

Validator then executes a single bundled nonzero MT-109 route matrix covering AC-109-1 through AC-109-3 and every authorization negative above against isolated Handshake-managed SurrealDB/EventLedger state.

Validator executes the current SurrealDB-corrected equivalents of PT-109-1 through PT-109-4 and focused cargo check with no PostgreSQL/SQLite dependency, fixture, DSN, fallback, mock-only authority, privileged-session ordinary flow, repo-local target, or zero-test result.

PASS_V8 is legal only when the shared predecessor and every MT-109 route family pass at the same candidate state; a route-local shim, frontend-supplied claims, process-token-as-account shortcut, or Flight-Recorder-only fix remains FAIL.
